text:
Tampa Bay probably played the game that deserved better than a four-goal loss. By the numbers, the Lightning were a coin flip with the Rangers at 51 percent to win in a full replay, and they out-attempted New York 63 to 52. The difference was a goaltending gap that grew as the night went on.

Pavel Dorofeyev and Mika Zibanejad set the tone early. Zibanejad opened the scoring on the power play at 5:34 of the first, and Dorofeyev made it 2-0 at 10:51. Tampa carried the first period in chance quality (1.06 expected goals to 0.58), but trailed anyway. Eeli Tolvanen then made it 3-0 on a shot with a 4 percent chance of going in, and Nikita Kucherov answered with a backhand of the same value. Andrei Vasilevskiy allowed four goals on 2.55 expected, about 1.45 goals worse than a typical goalie facing those shots.

Igor Shesterkin was the other side of it. He faced 24 shots, allowed one, and finished 1.59 goals better than expected, which earned him first star. The Rangers took over after the first, outchancing Tampa 1.60 to 0.84 in the second and 1.50 to 0.69 in the third. Gabe Perreault tipped in a fourth at 16:01 of the second, and Shesterkin added an empty-netter at 17:26 of the third for the 5-1 final. New York went 1 for 2 on the power play while Tampa went 0 for 7.
